Overview / TLDR

For modeling the signed error on the Y-axis, we ran the following models:

  • Lomax
  • Exponential
  • Weibull — this is the best-performing one.
  • Log-Normal
  • Gamma

For later fitting purposes, we also modeled the signed error on the X-axis to obtain hyper-priors.

Set up

Read in data and relevant scales:

Code 
task_df <- read_rds(here("data", "part1", "task.rds"))
participants <- read_rds(here("data", "part1", "participants.rds"))
exp1_x <- make_va_scale(data_min = -5, data_max = 5, px_min = 50, px_max = 585)
exp1_y <- make_va_scale(data_min = 0, data_max = 1, px_min = 410, px_max = 15)

Load data specific for this task:

Code 
task2_df <- task_df %>%
  filter(task == "task2") %>%
  select(-slider.x, -slider.y) %>%
  mutate(
    data.ans.x = param.mu,
    data.ans.y = dsgt(
      param.mu,
      param.mu,
      param.sigma,
      param.lambda,
      param.p,
      param.q,
      mean.cent = FALSE
    ),
    data.left.grad = numDeriv::grad(
      dsgt,
      param.mu - 1,
      mu = param.mu,
      sigma = param.sigma,
      lambda = param.lambda,
      p = param.p,
      q = param.q,
      mean.cent = FALSE
    ),
    data.right.grad = numDeriv::grad(
      dsgt,
      param.mu + 1,
      mu = param.mu,
      sigma = param.sigma,
      lambda = param.lambda,
      p = param.p,
      q = param.q,
      mean.cent = FALSE
    ),
  ) %>%
  right_join(participants, by = join_by(participantId)) %>%
  # calculate things related to participants' selection
  mutate(
    va.resp.x = exp1_x$px_to_va(pixel.select.x, dist_to_screen, pixelToMM),
    va.resp.y = exp1_y$px_to_va(pixel.select.y, dist_to_screen, pixelToMM),
    va.ans.x = exp1_x$data_to_va(data.ans.x, dist_to_screen, pixelToMM),
    va.ans.y = exp1_y$data_to_va(data.ans.y, dist_to_screen, pixelToMM),
  ) %>%
  mutate(flat = (abs(data.left.grad) + abs(data.right.grad)) / 2)

Error on Y

Error on Y, Lomax distribution

Wikipedia. Note that alpha is shape and lambda is scale. This is the stan reference. Math model:

\[ \begin{align*}\text{error}_i &\sim \text{Lomax}(\lambda_{\text{PID}[i]}, \alpha_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ \log(\lambda_j) &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\lambda, \sigma_\lambda^2) \\ \log(\alpha_j) &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\alpha, \sigma_\alpha^2) \\ \mu_\lambda, \mu_\alpha &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ \sigma_\lambda, \sigma_\alpha &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1) \end{align*} \]

# Define the Lomax family
lomax_family <- custom_family(
  "lomax",
  dpars = c("mu", "lambda", "alpha"), # parameters: lambda = scale, alpha = shape
  links = c("identity", "log", "log"), # log links ensure parameters are positive
  lb = c(-Inf, 0, 0), # lower bounds for both parameters
  type = "real"
)

# The Stan code for the Pareto log-likelihood function
# Note: Stan already has a built-in pareto_lpdf function
stan_funs <- "
  // Use the built-in pareto_type_2_lpdf function
  real lomax_lpdf(real y, real mu, real lambda, real alpha) {
    return pareto_type_2_lpdf(y | 0, lambda, alpha);
  }
  
  real lomax_rng(real mu, real lambda, real alpha) {
    return pareto_type_2_rng(0, lambda, alpha);
  }
"

Formula and posterior:

Formula and Posterior
f <- bf(
  error.y ~ 0,
  mu ~ 0,
  lambda ~ (1 | participantId),
  alpha ~ (1 | participantId),
  family = lomax_family
)

p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = alpha),
  prior(cauchy(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = alpha, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = lambda),
  prior(cauchy(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = lambda, lb = 0)
)

Fit the model:

model.y.lomax <- task2_df %>%
  mutate(error.y = abs(va.ans.y - va.resp.y)) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    family = lomax_family,
    prior = p,
    stanvars = stanvar(scode = stan_funs, block = "functions"),
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task2.y.lomax"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    iter = 10000,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15),
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
  )

Check fit and posterior check:

Perform posterior predictive checks:

Code 
expose_functions(model.y.lomax, vectorize = TRUE)

# Define the posterior_predict function in R as per the following vignette
# https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/brms/vignettes/brms_customfamilies.html
posterior_predict_lomax <- function(i, draws, ...) {
  lambda <- draws$dpars$lambda[i]
  alpha <- draws$dpars$alpha[i]
  lomax_rng(0, lambda, alpha)
}

# define custom log likelihood function for loo comparison

log_lik_lomax <- function(i, prep) {
  mu <- brms::get_dpar(prep, "mu", i = i)
  lambda <- brms::get_dpar(prep, "lambda", i = i)
  alpha <- brms::get_dpar(prep, "alpha", i = i)
  y <- prep$data$Y[i]

  # Lomax log-density: log(alpha) - log(lambda) - (alpha+1) * log(1 + y/lambda)
  log(alpha) - log(lambda) - (alpha + 1) * log1p(y / lambda)
}
pp_check(model.y.lomax, ndraws = 100)
pp_check(model.y.lomax, ndraws = 100, type = "pit_ecdf")

From the PIT-ECDF check it seems that indeed the lomax model is not a good one, because a well-calibrated model should show the line following the 45 degree line, not a flat line from above.

Error on Y, Exponential Distribution

Math model:

\[ \begin{align*}\text{error}_i &\sim \text{Exponential}(\lambda_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ \log(\lambda_j) &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\lambda, \sigma_\lambda) \\ \mu_\lambda &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1), \\ \sigma_\lambda &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1) \end{align*} \]

Formula and prior:

f <- bf(
  error.y ~ 0,
  mu ~ (1 | participantId), # technically this is lambda but we call it mu nonetheless
  family = exponential
)

# mu has log-link, so we don't pose any bounds on it
p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(cauchy(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0)
)

Fit the model:

model.y.exponential <- task2_df %>%
  mutate(error.y = abs(va.ans.y - va.resp.y)) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task2.y.exponential"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
    iter = 6000,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
  )

Check fit and posterior:

Error on Y, Weibull

Math formula:

\[ \begin{align} \texttt{error}_i &\sim \text{Weibull}(\mu_{\text{PID}[i]}, k_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ \log(\mu_j) &= \alpha_j \\ \log(k_j) &= \beta_j \\ \alpha_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\alpha, \sigma_\alpha) \\ \beta_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\beta, \sigma_\beta) \\ \mu_\alpha, \mu_\beta &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ \sigma_\alpha, \sigma_beta &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1) \end{align} \]

Specify formula and prior:

f <- bf(
  error.y ~ 0,
  mu ~ (1 | participantId), # log link
  shape ~ (1 | participantId), # log link
  family = weibull()
)

p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = shape),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = shape, lb = 0)
)

Fit the model:

model.y.weibull <- task2_df %>%
  mutate(error.y = va.ans.y - va.resp.y) %>%
  mutate(error.y = ifelse(error.y < tolerance, tolerance, error.y)) %>% # Weibull needs value to be > 0
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task2.y.weibull"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
    iter = 6000
  )

Check fit and posterior:

Error on Y, Log-Normal

Math formula: \[ \begin{align*} \texttt{error.y}_i &\sim \text{Log-Normal}(\mu_{\text{PID}[i]},\ \sigma_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ \mu_j &= \alpha_j \\ \log(\sigma_j) &= \beta_j \\ \alpha_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\alpha,\ \tau_\alpha) \\ \beta_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\beta,\ \tau_\beta) \\ \mu_\alpha,\ \mu_\beta &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ \tau_\alpha,\ \tau_\beta &\sim \mathcal{N}^{+}(0, 1) \end{align*} \]

Specify formula and prior:

f <- bf(
  error.y ~ 0,
  mu ~ (1 | participantId),
  sigma ~ (1 | participantId),
  family = lognormal()
)

p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = sigma),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = sigma, lb = 0)
)
model.y.lognormal <- task2_df %>%
  mutate(error.y = va.ans.y - va.resp.y) %>%
  mutate(error.y = ifelse(error.y < tolerance, tolerance, error.y)) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task2.y.lognormal"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
    iter = 6000
  )

Check fit and posterior:

Error on Y, Gamma

Math formula:

\[ \begin{align*} \texttt{error.y}_i &\sim \text{Gamma}(\mu_{\text{PID}[i]},\ k_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ \mu_j &= \alpha_j^{-1} \\ \log(k_j) &= \beta_j \\ \alpha_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\alpha,\ \tau_\alpha) \\ \beta_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\beta,\ \tau_\beta) \\ \mu_\alpha,\ \mu_\beta &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ \tau_\alpha,\ \tau_\beta &\sim \mathcal{N}^{+}(0, 1) \end{align*} \]

Specify formula and prior:

f <- bf(
  error.y ~ 0,
  mu ~ (1 | participantId),
  shape ~ (1 | participantId),
  family = Gamma()
)

p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = shape),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = shape, lb = 0)
)
model.y.gamma <- task2_df %>%
  mutate(error.y = va.ans.y - va.resp.y) %>%
  mutate(error.y = ifelse(error.y < tolerance, tolerance, error.y)) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task2.y.gamma"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
    iter = 6000
  )

Note that the above have a lot of divergent transitions, even though we took adapt_delta = 0.99, suggesting that this is a bad posterior fit, and that this is not the right model.

Nevertheless, we check its posterior fit for completeness:

LOO Comparison

Note that we won’t use Gamma in the model comparison, because the models have divergent transitions after fitting and demonstrate poor calibration.

Loo comparison:

brms::loo(
  model.y.lomax,
  model.y.exponential,
  model.y.lognormal,
  model.y.weibull,
  moment_match = TRUE,
  reloo = FALSE,
  cores = parallel::detectCores()
)

See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.

Model comparisons:
                    elpd_diff se_diff
model.y.weibull        0.0       0.0 
model.y.lognormal    -46.5       8.0 
model.y.lomax        -69.7      16.5 
model.y.exponential -177.4      46.7

Weibull is the best model.

Error on X, Normal distribution

Math model:

\[ \begin{align} \texttt{error\_va}_{i} &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\text{PID[i]}, \sigma_{\text{PID[i]}}^2) \\ \mu_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\bar{\mu}, \bar{\sigma}^2), j \in [16] \\ \sigma_j &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(\alpha, \beta^2), j \in [16] \\ \bar{\mu}, \alpha &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)\\ \bar{\sigma}, \beta &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1) \end{align} \]

Formula and prior:

f <- bf(
  error.x ~ 0,
  mu ~ (1 | participantId),
  sigma ~ (1 | participantId),
  family = gaussian
)

# sigma has log-link, so we don't pose any bounds on it
p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = sigma),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = sigma, lb = 0)
)

Fit the model:

model.x.normal <- task2_df %>%
  mutate(error.x = va.resp.x - va.ans.x) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task2.x.normal"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
    iter = 6000,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
  )

Check fit and posterior:

summary(model.x.normal)

and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential

Important

Get the posterior for fitting another operator (i.e., BisectArea):

# model.x.normal %>% get_variables(.)

model.x.normal %>%
  spread_draws(b_Intercept, b_sigma_Intercept) %>%
  mutate(b_sigma = exp(b_sigma_Intercept)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(b_Intercept, b_sigma)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = name)) +
  stat_halfeye()
model.x.normal %>%
  spread_draws(b_Intercept, b_sigma_Intercept) %>%
  mutate(b_sigma = exp(b_sigma_Intercept)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(b_Intercept, b_sigma)) %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  median_qi(value, .width = c(0.66, 0.95))

From error on Y to error on X

Create a dataframe for the “average participant”:

Code 
avg_pixelToMM <- participants %>% pull(pixelToMM) %>% mean(.)
avg_distToScreen <- participants %>% pull(dist_to_screen) %>% mean(.)
avg_participant <- tibble(
  pixelToMM = avg_pixelToMM,
  distToScreen = avg_distToScreen,
  participantId = "avg_participant"
)

avg_participant

Create dataframe for average participant and do posterior draws:

# Y-error draws in visual angle space
y_draws <- avg_participant %>%
  add_predicted_draws(
    model.y.weibull,
    re_formula = NULL, # include random effects
    allow_new_levels = TRUE,
    seed = 1
  )

Plot the marginalized example to use for paper

So here are the parameters of the particular example we’re looking at: \(\mu = -1.1, \sigma = 0.9, \lambda = -0.3, p = 2.6, q = 2.17\). The highest point has x coordinate -1.1 and y coordinate dsgt(-1.1, ...).

Code 
x <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 100)
y <- dsgt(
  x,
  mu = -1.1,
  sigma = 0.9,
  lambda = -0.3,
  p = 2.6,
  q = 2.17,
  mean.cent = FALSE
)

x_val = -1.1
y_val = dsgt(
  x_val,
  mu = -1.1,
  sigma = 0.9,
  lambda = -0.3,
  p = 2.6,
  q = 2.17,
  mean.cent = FALSE
)

example_plot <- tibble(x = x, y = y) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_line() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_tidybayes() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = x_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = y_val,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray"
  )
example_plot
Code 
# specific pdf we're working with
f <- function(x) {
  dsgt(
    x,
    mu = -1.1,
    sigma = 0.9,
    lambda = -0.3,
    p = 2.6,
    q = 2.17,
    mean.cent = FALSE
  )
}

va.ans.y <- exp1_y$data_to_va(y_val, avg_distToScreen, avg_pixelToMM)

# here we go from errors on y to errors on x
x_errors <- y_draws %>%
  mutate(
    va.pred.y = va.ans.y - .prediction,
    num.pred.y = exp1_y$va_to_data(va.pred.y, avg_distToScreen, avg_pixelToMM),
    eps_data = y_val - num.pred.y
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x_left = uniroot(function(x) f(x) - num.pred.y, c(-5, x_val))$root,
    x_right = uniroot(function(x) f(x) - num.pred.y, c(x_val, 5))$root,
    # random flip betwee x_left and x_right
    num.pred.x = if (sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 1)) x_left else x_right
  )

So we will use this plot as our example for things to marginalize.

Code 
theme_set(theme_tidybayes(base_size = 10))

x_graph <- x_errors %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num.pred.x)) +
  stat_slab() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0) +
  labs(x = "", y = "density")

y_graph <- x_errors %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = num.pred.y)) +
  stat_slab() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0) +
  labs(x = "density", y = "")

Use patchwork to put things together:

library(patchwork)

new_output <- example_plot +
  y_graph +
  x_graph +
  plot_spacer() +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 2,
    nrow = 2,
    widths = c(4, 0.5),
    heights = c(3, 0.5)
  )

new_output

Error on y is too hard to see, so we also create a zoomed-in version of it:

  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.45, 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "") +
  # theme_tidybayes(base_size = 6) +
